title.en: Compute the mean deviation about the mean
Compute the mean deviation about the median

say.en: The deviations from the mean always add up to zero, so we cannot just average them. Taking absolute values fixes this. In this lesson: Compute the mean deviation about the mean.
Compute the mean deviation about the median.

body.en: The *mean deviation* about a central value $a$ is the mean of the absolute deviations: $\text{M.D.}(a) = \frac1n\sum|x_i - a|$. It is usually found about the mean $\bar x$ or the median M. (The mean deviation is least when it is taken about the median.)
body.kn: ಪ್ರತಿ ಬೆಲೆಯ ಸರಾಸರಿ ಅಥವಾ ಮಧ್ಯಾಂಕದಿಂದ ದೂರವನ್ನು ಚಿಹ್ನೆ ಬಿಟ್ಟು ತೆಗೆದು, ಆ ದೂರಗಳ ಸರಾಸರಿ ಕಂಡುಹಿಡಿಯಿರಿ. ಇದೇ ಸರಾಸರಿ ವಿಚಲನೆ.

narration.en: Here are eight observations on a number line: 6, 7, 10, 12, 13, 4, 8 and 12.

say.en: Here are eight observations on a number line: 6, 7, 10, 12, 13, 4, 8 and 12.
Their sum is 72, so the mean is 9. Mean deviation measures the average distance of the values from this centre.
Take each distance from 9, ignoring the sign: 3, 2, 1, 3, 4, 5, 1, 3. They add up to 22.
Divide by the number of observations: the mean deviation about the mean is 22 over 8, which is 2.75.

vars.name: MDa
vars.expr: (abs(3 - a_x) + abs(5 - a_x) + abs(6 - a_x) + abs(7 - a_x) + abs(9 - a_x) + abs(12 - a_x) + abs(v - a_x))/7

vars.name: MDmean
vars.expr: (abs(3 - mean) + abs(5 - mean) + abs(6 - mean) + abs(7 - mean) + abs(9 - mean) + abs(12 - mean) + abs(v - mean))/7

shapes.fn: (abs(3 - x) + abs(5 - x) + abs(6 - x) + abs(7 - x) + abs(9 - x) + abs(12 - x) + abs(v - x))/7

say.en: Let us solve this together. Find the mean deviation about the mean of 6, 7, 10, 12, 13, 4, 8, 12.
x̄ = 72 over 8 equals 9.
|x i minus 9|: 3, 2, 1, 3, 4, 5, 1, 3; their sum is 22.
M.D. = 22 over 8 equals 2.75.
So the answer is 2.75.

Arrange: 3, 3, 4, 5, 7, 9, 10, 12, 18, 19, 21; n equals 11, so the median is the 6th value, 9.
M.D. = 58 over 11 is approximately 5.27.
So the answer is 58 over 11 is approximately 5.27.
